title: Targets the City set for itself, and whether they were met
question: For services delivered mainly by nonprofits, what did the City say it would achieve each year, and did it?
finding: The City publishes yearly targets for 65 measures of services that nonprofits mostly deliver. Across 399 measure-years with both a target and a result, 56% met the target; in FY2024-25, 37 of 65 did (57%). Every measure met its target at least once, but 10 are on an unbroken run of three or more missed years that was still running in FY2024-25; the longest run is 11 years (Percentage of graffiti requests abated within 48 hours (public property), FY2014-15 to FY2024-25).
how: Every measure in the Controller's Citywide Performance Metrics dataset was read. Those kept cover homelessness, housing placement, shelter, behavioural health and treatment, workforce, children and youth, early childhood, seniors' meals and community services, re-entry services and street cleaning; the list and the direction counted as better are written out in the script. A year counts as met when the full-year result reached the target (at or above for measures where higher is better, at or below where lower is better). Caseload measures, whose targets are forecasts, are left out.
limits: These are the City's own numbers about whole programmes, not about any one organization, and the departments report their own results to the Controller. A missed target can mean the target was set too high, that need grew faster than money, or that the pandemic closed services: fiscal years 2020 and 2021 are in the series and marked in the next screen. The dataset keeps only measures that are still current, so a measure retired before 2026 does not appear at all; the homelessness department replaced all of its measures in fiscal year 2023, which is why its series are short. Street cleaning is done mostly by City crews.
